title-proc.eng: DCC Contract for Construction of the Coolock to Clontarf Active Travel Scheme Section 2 – Gracefield Road to Vernon Avenue

description-proc.eng: Dublin City Council aims to enhance the quality of life for its residents by developing an integrated Active Travel Network. This comprehensive network is designed to foster connections among individuals via pedestrian pathways, segregated cycle provision and other environmentally friendly transportation alternatives. The enhancement of accessibility and interconnectivity for people walking, wheeling and cycling within this network is anticipated to play a pivotal role in mitigating carbon emissions originating from transport activities. The Council’s objective is to augment the existing 40km network into a seamlessly connected 314km network spanning the entire city. The Gracefield Road to Vernon Avenue Active Travel Scheme is one of the projects identified under this initiative. Gracefield Road, Brookwood Avenue, Sybil Hill Road and Vernon Avenue have been identified as suitable roads for active travel measures. This scheme will deliver protected cycling facilities in both directions and numerous improvements for pedestrians over a 2.6km route along these roads, between the junctions with Malahide Road and Seafield Road. The scheme includes the provision of segregated cycle facilities, improved pedestrian facilities (footpath and junction upgrades), ducting, resurfacing, etc.. The scheme also includes the upgrade of seven signal-controlled junctions to improve pedestrian and cyclist facilities. The scheme comprises the following: - Reconfiguration of existing carriageway for inclusion of protected cycle lanes - Site clearance - Pavement works - Kerbs and footways - Traffic islands - Public lighting - Traffic signs and road markings - Drainage works - Traffic signals and ducting - Utilities - Landscaping and urban realm works - Bike stands - Temporary traffic management. For further information, please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie; CfT ID 8916766. Please note that this project is subject to funding.

description-proc.eng: As part of its ongoing efforts to pursue its sustainable development goals and achieve the ambitions set out by the Government in its vision for 2035, Cameroon adopted in 2020, to implement the second phase of its vision covering the period 2020-2030, a policy document entitled the National Development Strategy 2020-2030 (SND30). During this phase, the Government intends to bring about the structural transformation of the economy through industrialisation. However, achieving these objectives will require well-structured measures designed to minimise the impact on the environment, particularly in light of the growing momentum of environmental protection initiatives promoted within the framework of the various Conferences of the Parties on climate change (COP), the most recent of which (COP 31) was held in Recife, Brazil, from 10. - 21. November 2025. With a view to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals, Cameroon has joined the Central African Forest Initiative (CAFI), which aims to recognise and preserve the value of the region"s forests in order to mitigate climate change and reduce poverty. More specifically, the long-term objective of the Cameroon-CAFI partnership is to facilitate the acceleration of economic development by promoting the application of the principle of a "green economy" through which Cameroonian value chains are made competitive and meet the demands of international, national and sub-regional markets, whilst Cameroon ensures food security and reduces the impact of the development of these sectors on deforestation and forest degradation. This is in line with the principles set out in the SND30 and defined in the Letter of Intent (LOI) signed between Cameroon and CAFI in October 2024 with a view to realising the ambitions outlined in the sectoral strategies and will underpin the success of the future partnership. In order to facilitate the consolidation and implementation of the Letter of Intent signed for a long-term partnership between Cameroon and CAFI, the partners have decided to envisage a three-year pilot phase. Furthermore, it was decided to implement a sectoral and multi-level coordination project, which will also oversee the portfolio management and coordination of three technical projects funded by CAFI. Its aim will be to strengthen the capacities of national technical bodies for enhanced and inclusive cross-sectoral coordination, and for strategic and spatial planning, in order to move towards a green economy. This coordination aims to build consensus on the planning tools to be developed, the reforms to be implemented and the innovative financing mechanisms for the development of the green economy, which will help to increase the mobilisation and alignment of interventions and funding from the public and private sectors, both national and international.

title-proc.eng: Framework agreement for painting and painting products.

description-proc.eng: Background Arendal municipality shall establish a new framework agreement for painting services and painting products for use in municipal buildings and properties. The contract shall primarily cover the needs of Arendal Eiendom, and it shall also be used by Arendal Church Council and the Arendal Harbour. The procurement will be carried out as the existing contract expires and as the municipality needs a more appropriate contract structure that separates the executing services and procurements of goods for work under it's own auspices. The aim is to ensure good need coverage, predictable access to capacity, efficient ordering and better follow-up of procurements and assignments. The municipality has a continual need for painting, equipment and consumables, as well as painting, wallpapering and floor laying services in connection with maintenance, upgrading and minor renovation works. The need varies between the entities and over time, and it is therefore important to have a framework agreement that provides flexibility, quick response and good delivery security. At the same time, the municipality would like a system that supports a clear interface between assignments that are carried out by an external supplier and products that are purchased for the municipality ́s own use. This shall contribute to more uniform practice, better cost control and simple contract follow-up. Description of the assignment The procurement is for a framework agreement for painting services and painting products for Arendal municipality and associated entities. The framework agreement includes both the procurement of services and the procurement of goods for use in the municipality's ongoing operation and maintenance. The assignment is divided into two sub-contracts. Sub-contract 1 includes painting, wallpapering and floor laying services, including necessary materials and equipment included in the execution of the assignment. Sub-contract 2 includes paint, put-offs, consumables and the accompanying equipment for the municipality ́s own use for work under its own auspices. The service part shall cover both internal and external work, and will mainly include maintenance, minor upgrades and renovation work in municipal purpose-built buildings. The product part shall cover the standard need for paint products and the accompanying equipment for use in the municipality ́s own work assignments. A delivery is requested that gives the municipality access to relevant professional competence, the necessary capacity and suitable products within the contract ́s extent. The framework agreement shall facilitate a practical and clear ordering model, so that both service assignments and goods procurements can be carried out in an efficient and predictable way.

description-proc.deu: Der Auftrag betrifft das Projekt „Next-intl“, das die Sicherheitsoptimierung von „next-intl“ umfasst, einer weit verbreiteten Open-Source-Bibliothek zur Entwicklung mehrsprachiger Anwendungen mit Next.js. Dabei wird ein iterativer Ansatz verfolgt, wobei gleichzeitig eine nachhaltige Wartung für die Zukunft gewährleistet wird. In vierzehn Arbeitspaketen umfassen die Leistungen die Bewertung und Behebung von Sicherheitsrisiken, die Entwicklung und Validierung einer modernen Infrastruktur für Builds, Tests und Benchmarking, die Anpassung der Bibliothek an neue Next.js-Funktionen und JavaScript-Standards, die Entwicklung automatisierter Übersetzungsworkflows sowie die Vorbereitung und das Testen einer neuen Hauptversion. Der Auftrag umfasst zudem technische Refaktorisierung, systematische Verbesserungen der Dokumentationsinfrastruktur und der Governance für die Maintainer*innen. Ziel ist es, die Sicherheit, Funktionalität und langfristige Nachhaltigkeit einer Komponente zu stärken, die es Hunderttausenden von Webdiensten ermöglicht, Menschen in ihrer eigenen Sprache zu erreichen.
description-proc.eng: The contract concerns the project Next-intl, which covers security hardening of next-intl, a widely used open-source library for building multilingual applications with Next.js., using an iterative approach while ensuring sustainable maintenance for the future in the process. Across fourteen work packages, the services include assesing and addressing security risks; developing and validating modern build, testing, and benchmarking infrastructure; adapting the library to new Next.js features and JavaScript standards; developing automated translation workflows; and preparing and testing a new major version. The contract also covers technical refactoring, systematic improvements for the documentation infrastructure and maintainer governance. Its aim is to strengthen the security, functionality, and long-term sustainability of a component that enables hundreds of thousands of web services to reach people in their own languages.

The system bears the mark that it has lived for almost 10 years. There are some technical debts that we need help cleaning up. Part of this is moving some internal APIs, which have been made available with MID-server, over to exposed facade services which are more responsive. The ITSM module is used to a very large degree by IT Operations, but also on customer service, dealer services (incident) and in Security. ServiceDesk receives cases via the user portal, chat, telephone, attendance and e-mails that are automatically registered in ServiceNow. The case types they work with are primarily incident and request. It is a well developed Change management with a number of automated standard changes. ServiceNow is receiving more and more changes via pipeline or other integrations from internal Jira. The operational centre is the escalation point for general errors in the systems. They have monitoring and use, among other things, Splunk to receive events. Emphasis will be put on the tenderer ́s experience and competence in addition to operation and maintenance. Tenderers shall be a proactive consultant for the entire spectrum of services the contract covers. Whether there is new functionality in ServiceNow, a need for clearing in technical debts, smart choices around integrations, utilisation of functionality in the existing system based on the supplier knowing NP's business needs or the like. Requirements that shall be met. Norsk Tipping has organised development work in a product development model. The Customer Support product area is responsible for i.a. management and further development of ServiceNow, Genesys Cloud and self-service systems. Developers and consultants from the chosen supplier in this procurement will be important resources in this team together with other internal and external resources. NT has few, but good internal resources with competence in ServiceNow, and it is important to have a professional supplier that provides me good access to resources and who can contribute with expert help. As a starting point, the team consists of a system manager/owner and two system administrators, one of whom is defined as a team architect. The product development area currently consists of two multi-disciplinary teams, but which share internal resources and to a large degree work across. The product development manager has management responsibility for the teams and has, in addition, a team management role for the teams, in order to ensure progress and prioritising tasks. The product area is responsible for the management assignments being carried out and together prioritise small and large assignments based on the company principles for product development. The product development area follows the company ́s development cycle together with the other 12 areas and a joint plan is carried out at a general level, approx. 3 times per annum. The detailed planning will mainly be carried out in 2-week sprinters. Errors that occur are continually corrected as well as ongoing work in the other processes. The tenderer is expected to have competence in the following main areas. The list is not exhaustive: ·         ServiceNow platform ·         Licenses ·         Administration ·         Development ·         Integrations and integration security ·         Active and proactive consulting (ServiceNow and technology/architecture) ·         Coordination and planning ·         Work in multi-disciplinary teams ·         SLA and support Norsk Tipping currently has an agreement with DXC for ServiceNow. description-proc.eng: The DigiTVET project is an initiative within the German development cooperation programme "Vocational Education and Training in Jordan" aimed at enhancing Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) in Jordan through digital transformation. The project seeks to improve the accessibility, quality, and relevance of TVET in alignment with the demands of the modern labour market. The overarching goal is to empower the Jordanian Ministry of Education (MoE) and related stakeholders to adopt inclusive, labour market-oriented digital methods in vocational education. The project addresses critical challenges in the Jordanian TVET system, particularly the lack of structured governance and implementation capacities for high-quality digital vocational training. By leveraging insights from previous initiatives, DigiTVET aims to foster a cohesive approach to digital education, ensuring that methodologies are tailored to the needs of diverse target groups, including women and marginalized communities. Key objectives include the establishment of standardised procedures for integrating digital tools, standards and methods into the ministry, enhancing the competencies of educators and management staff, and developing inclusive digital teaching and learning offerings. By focusing on these areas, DigiTVET will contribute significantly to Jordan's 2030 Agenda, particularly in advancing sustainable economic development and inclusive education. The expected outcomes of the DigiTVET project include improved governance of digital vocational training, increased participation of disadvantaged groups, and the establishment of a robust framework for ongoing capacity development within the TVET sector. The module is structured into three outputs: Output 1 aims to develop procedures and structures that improve the use and integration of digital methods at MoE. Output 2 aims to support the development of digital competencies and skills of teachers and managers. Output 3 aims to support selected TVET providers to develop and pilot digital teaching and learning offers in cooperation with private sector and civil society partners, with a focus on disadvantaged groups and regions, including in particular BTEC graduates.

title-proc.eng: Central Laboratory Services for Clinical Trial

description-proc.eng: The Federal Agency for Disruptive Innovation - SPRIND GmbH ("SPRIND") - aims to create new disruptive innovations from Germany. That means products, services and systems that make all our lives noticeably and sustainably better. To achieve this, SPRIND brings together new thinkers from science and business, people with outstanding ideas, special expertise, and passion. Hence, SPRIND provides an entrepreneurial environment that turns ideas into reality. The objective of BiconY Therapeutics GmbH, a SPRIND subsidiary, is the development of a bispecific antibody combination for the treatment of solid tumours. The combination consists of proprietary, bispecific CD3 anti-bodies (bsAbCD3) and bispecific CD28 co-stimulators (BiCos), which, when used together, significantly improve the specificity, sustainability, and efficiency of a T cell recruitment and thus the immune response against tumour cells. The aim of the research and development activities is to provide proof of concept for the effect of bispecific antibody therapy in the form of two phase I/IIa clinical trials. For the conduct of the planned phase I/IIa clinical trials, comprehensive central laboratory services are required for the collection logistics, processing, analysis, management, distribution and long-term storage of the biological specimens obtained from the trial participants. This includes in particular the analysis of cytokines in serum and the isolation of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC). Therefore, BiconY is looking for a service provider to act as central laboratory for these clinical trials. Please refer to the tender documents for further details.

title-proc.eng: Kunnskap om arbeidsinkludering i et arbeidsmarked og arbeidsliv i endring og omstilling. Invitasjon til markedsdialog.

description-proc.eng: Globalisering og megatrender har innvirkning på arbeidsmarked og arbeidsliv, og medfører behov for endring og omstilling. Raske teknologiske framskritt, demografiske endringer, klimaendringer og kriser som Covid-19 er eksempler på sentrale drivere for endring i samfunnet, og som både enkeltvis og samlet har konsekvenser for arbeidsmarked og arbeidsliv. Hvordan arbeidsmarkedet vil utvikle seg framover, og hvordan arbeidstakere og arbeidsgivere vil tilpasse seg disse endringene, er usikkert. Det er grunn til å tro at endringene vil ha innvirkning på forvaltningens organisering og gjennomføringsevne, og det er usikkert hvilke tiltak og virkemidler som framover vil være de mest effektive for å bidra til arbeidsinkludering og høy arbeidsdeltakelse. Alle som kan jobbe skal få mulighet til å jobbe. Arbeids- og inkluderingsdepartementet (AID) ønsker kunnskap om hvordan store samfunnsendringer, utviklingstrekk og omstillinger i det norske arbeidsmarkedet og arbeidslivet har innvirkning på arbeidsdeltakelse og arbeidsinkludering. Det er behov for kunnskap om hvordan tiltak og virkemidler fungerer i en slik kontekst. Det er videre behov for kunnskap om grupper som i dag er vurdert til å være utsatt på arbeidsmarkedet, og hvordan situasjonen for disse vil kunne bli framover. Omstillinger kan ramme ulikt. For noen kan omstilling bidra til inkludering i arbeid, mens for andre kan omstilling føre til ekskludering fra arbeid. Det er også usikkert om grupper som vi i dag vurderer som utsatt på arbeidsmarkedet vil være det framover, eller om dette vil endre seg og om det er andre grupper som kommer til. Det finnes mye kunnskap, og det er over mange år iverksatt en rekke tiltak og virkemidler for å få flere og særlig utsatte grupper i arbeid. Det er imidlertid behov for helhetlig og mer systematisk kunnskap om hvordan endringer og omstilling treffer disse, og hvordan tiltak og virkemidler enkeltvis og samlet fungerer nå og framover. I denne veiledende kunngjøringen inviterer vi forskningsmiljøer til å komme med innspill til rammer for et FoU-prosjekt som kan gi oss relevant og helhetlig kunnskap om hvordan endringer og omstillinger i arbeidsmarked og arbeidsliv på kort og lang sikt treffer utsatte grupper, virksomheter, forvaltning og tjenester, og hvordan flest mulig kan inkluderes i arbeid.

title-proc.eng: Auftragsänderung 1: Sahel Resilience Strengthening (SARES)

description-proc.eng: The Sahel region is facing multiple crises, facing high levels of acute and chronic food insecurity and malnutrition, widespread poverty, and unequal access to basic social services. Due to particularly strong gender inequalities in the Sahel, women are more affected by these challenges than men. Whilst agriculture remains the backbone of rural livelihoods, yields are low and over a third of crops are lost every year. Agricultural livelihoods become more and more precarious in an environment characterised by land degradation, increasing temperatures, recurrent droughts, floods, as well as erratic rainfall. The presence of refugees and internally displaced persons (IDPs) increases the pressure on natural resources as well as on basic infrastructure in accessible areas, increasing conflicts over the use of natural resources. Climate change furthers food insecurity, threatens livelihoods and strengthens drivers of conflict. The transitional development assistance (TDA) project Sahel Resilience Strengthening (SARES) has been conceived to complement the Sahel Resilience Initiative (SRI) in selected intervention areas in four Sahelian countries (Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger, and Chad). The parallel commissioning entails the opportunity to build on the comparative strengths of the three organisations WFP, UNICEF, and GIZ along the Humanitarian-Development-Peace (HDP) Nexus. SARES therefore works in the same geographic areas with overlapping target groups. The project strengthens local capacities for natural resource governance (NRG), the resolution of NRG related conflicts, and disaster risk management. Building on stabilisation measures, it supports food and nutrition security through a livelihood approach and promotes social cohesion. The project implements key elements of BMZ"s Strategy on Transitional Development Assistance. It addresses three of the strategies in four fields of action: food and nutrition security, disaster risk management, as well as peaceful and inclusive communities. The project complements WFP"s and UNICEF"s measures to build stabilization capacities by focusing on adaptation and transformation capacities of individuals and communities. The capacities of local structures to govern natural resources effectively and inclusively, and to resolve related conflicts are strengthened, to help these structures to adapt to changing contexts (effects of climate change, effects of forced displacement etc.) and to transform rules in this area (e.g., reduce discriminatory regulations, improve access to land and other resources for women). The capacities of communities to adapt to increasing conflicts of interest between population groups, especially in communities hosting internally displaced persons (IDP) and suffering from increased pressure on local resources, are strengthened. This allows communities to organize community dialogues and to identify community measures that create or strengthen connections between (potentially) conflicting groups. Farmers" and agro-pastoralists" individual adaptation and transformation capacities to further diversify their production, to make it more nutrient-sensitive, to store, process, and market their products are strengthened through respective trainings and by providing the necessary materials. Capacities of individuals and of producer groups or cooperatives to engage in secondary production are fostered through training, provision of equipment, and continuous coaching. Opportunities for secondary production are focused on youth and women without adequate access to land. Income generating activities and capacity development interventions are designed in a way that allows persons with disabilities to participate. Through complementary commissioning, the project facilitates inter-agency cooperation between WFP, UNICEF, and GIZ, and joint learning at the HDP-nexus. It fosters an adequate representation of women in local structures, in community dialogues, and in income generating activities.

The three objectives are: anticipating and managing change in the new world of work brought about by the green, digital and demographic transitions; improving prevention of workplace accidents and illnesses; increasing preparedness for any potential future health crises. The implementation of these three objectives is underpinned by: (i) social dialogue; (ii) strengthening of the evidence base; (iii) strengthening of enforcement; (iv) awareness raising; and (v) funding. At its plenary meeting in December 2025, the tripartite Advisory Committee on Safety and Health at Work (ACSH) adopted an opinion on the state of play and future impulses regarding the EU strategic framework on health and safety at work4. Moreover, in June 2026, the Commission adopted the Report on the screening of the EU acquis in the area of health and safety at work5, and its accompanying Staff Working Document6 [TBC]. title-proc.eng: Procurement of consultancy services for nuclear security, including handling used fuel, radiation protection and risk assessment.

description-proc.eng: The consultant agreement shall cover the provision of technical services in support of DSA ́s core functions within regulatory work. The work shall include reviewing and assessing technical documentation and support for DSA in connection with inspections. There are three nuclear plants in Norway: the research reactor facilities in Kjeller and Halden, and the combined landfill and storage facility for low and medium radioactive waste in Himdalen. In 2018 the Norwegian government established a new government organisation, Norsk Nukleærdekommisjonering (NND), which will take over all Norwegian nuclear power plants in Kjeller, Halden and Himdalen from the original operator, Institute for Energy Engineering (IFE). NND will be responsible for the operation of the nuclear installations, the production of them and the handling of radioactive waste and used core fuel. So far the nuclear power plant in Halden has been transferred from IFE to NND, and the other two installations are close to being transferred. Before the shutdown can start, there are a number of processes that must be completed so that the operator(s) shall be able to make changes in the installations in a safe and responsible manner, and for the regulation authority (DSA) to be able to approve changes in accordance with regulations and international standards. In preparation for the liquidation and during the shutdown, there will be a need to establish a new waste handling facility, including plans for a US-developed mobile melt consolidation facility (MMC). The procurement is covered by the Security Act and reflected in the contracting authority ́s requirement specifications and security requirements. Tenderers who would like to offer in this procurement are asked separately to familiarise themselves with the stated guidelines, prerequisites and requirements.
